scenes.visual: Title card 'One Cell, One Shipping Line' fades in over a single oval beta cell, drawn once and never redrawn for the rest of the film. THE WORLD, kept for both films: 16:9, warm cream background, flat cartoon shapes, labelled blocks, no molecular structures. COLOUR MAP, the same in every scene and in the second film: NUCLEUS = DEEP BLUE circle; ROUGH ER = TEAL folded ribbons dotted with small dark ribosome dots; GOLGI APPARATUS = ORANGE stack of curved flat sacs; VESICLES = GOLD small bubbles; CELL MEMBRANE = GREY outline of the cell; MITOCHONDRIA = RED beans; ATP = small YELLOW sparks; INSULIN or the marked protein = a GOLD glow; MESSENGER RNA = a short PURPLE strand. ROUTE STRIP, always at the top of the screen: 'nucleus (sends a copy) → ribosome on rough ER → vesicle → Golgi → vesicle → cell membrane'; the nucleus segment is PURPLE (messenger RNA travels), the rest GOLD (the protein travels); the current stop lights up. ENERGY: mitochondria feed a shared pool of YELLOW sparks labelled 'energy supply (schematic)'; never draw one spark delivered to one step. Anything not computed is labelled 'schematic'.

scenes.tts: The insulin gene never leaves a beta cell's nucleus. So how does insulin end up outside the cell? After a meal, your blood sugar rises, and beta cells in your pancreas release this protein hormone.
scenes.visual: A plate of food, then a small pancreas icon with one cell circled; zoom into that oval cell. The DEEP BLUE nucleus sits at left with a lock icon on it labelled 'gene stays here'. A GOLD glow appears outside the GREY membrane on the right with a question mark between the two. The route strip at top appears, all stops dim.
scenes.narration: The insulin gene never leaves a beta cell's nucleus. So how does insulin end up outside the cell? After a meal, your blood sugar rises, and beta cells in your pancreas release this protein hormone.

scenes.tts: Here is the answer in one picture. First a copy of the instructions travels, then the protein itself. Each part can only work on what the part before it hands over.
scenes.visual: A faint dashed line is sketched across the cell: a PURPLE dashed segment from the nucleus to the teal ER, then a GOLD dashed segment through a gold bubble, the orange Golgi and another gold bubble to the right-hand membrane. Small on-screen labels: 'copy of instructions' over the purple part, 'protein' over the gold part. A small purple strand runs the purple segment, then a small gold parcel appears at the ER and runs the gold segment, once, quickly. The line fades back to faint; it will be drawn for real stop by stop.
scenes.narration: Here is the answer in one picture. First a copy of the instructions travels, then the protein itself. Each part can only work on what the part before it hands over.

scenes.tts: Start in the nucleus. It holds most of the cell's D N A, its instructions. The gene for insulin is one stretch of that D N A. But the gene itself stays put.
scenes.caption: Start in the nucleus. It holds most of the cell's DNA, its instructions. The gene for insulin is one stretch of that DNA. But the gene itself stays put.
scenes.visual: Route strip: 'nucleus' lights up. Zoom into the DEEP BLUE nucleus: a long coiled thread labelled 'DNA'; one short segment highlights and is labelled 'insulin gene'. A small chain-and-lock icon pins the gene inside the nucleus.
scenes.narration: Start in the nucleus. It holds most of the cell's DNA, its instructions. The gene for insulin is one stretch of that DNA. But the gene itself stays put.

scenes.tts: Here is a puzzle for you. The gene stays locked in the nucleus. So what leaves the nucleus instead, carrying its instructions out?
scenes.visual: The highlighted gene glows inside the nucleus; an empty dotted outline of 'something' waits at the nuclear edge with a large question mark. A small on-screen timer ring begins.
scenes.narration: Here is a puzzle for you. The gene stays locked in the nucleus. So what leaves the nucleus instead, carrying its instructions out?

scenes.visual: Hold: the dotted outline at the nuclear edge pulses gently; timer ring fills over 5 seconds.

scenes.tts: A copy. The cell copies the gene into messenger R N A. That working copy leaves the nucleus and carries the instructions to the next stop.
scenes.caption: A copy. The cell copies the gene into messenger RNA. That working copy leaves the nucleus and carries the instructions to the next stop.
scenes.visual: A short PURPLE strand peels off the gene, labelled 'messenger RNA (a copy)'. It slides out through the edge of the nucleus while the gene stays behind. The GOLD route line draws from the nucleus toward the teal ER, following the purple strand.
scenes.narration: A copy. The cell copies the gene into messenger RNA. That working copy leaves the nucleus and carries the instructions to the next stop.

scenes.tts: The next stop is a ribosome on the rough E R. The E R is a set of folded membranes. On the rough E R, ribosomes dot the surface. A ribosome reads the messenger R N A and links building blocks into a protein chain. The chain threads into the E R, where it folds.
scenes.caption: The next stop is a ribosome on the rough ER. The ER is a set of folded membranes. On the rough ER, ribosomes dot the surface. A ribosome reads the messenger RNA and links building blocks into a protein chain. The chain threads into the ER, where it folds.
scenes.visual: Route strip: 'ribosome on rough ER' lights up. Zoom on the TEAL folded ribbons dotted with dark ribosome dots. The PURPLE strand runs through one ribosome dot; beads pop out one by one into a chain labelled 'protein chain', which snakes through the teal membrane into the space inside and folds into a compact GOLD-glowing shape. A soft YELLOW glow from the shared energy pool below brightens around the ER while the chain grows (schematic).
scenes.narration: The next stop is a ribosome on the rough ER. The ER is a set of folded membranes. On the rough ER, ribosomes dot the surface. A ribosome reads the messenger RNA and links building blocks into a protein chain. The chain threads into the ER, where it folds.

scenes.tts: Now the protein has to move. A vesicle, a small bubble of membrane, buds off the E R. It carries the protein across to the Golgi apparatus.
scenes.caption: Now the protein has to move. A vesicle, a small bubble of membrane, buds off the ER. It carries the protein across to the Golgi apparatus.
scenes.visual: Route strip: 'vesicle' lights up. A patch of teal membrane bulges, pinches off, and becomes a GOLD bubble with the glowing protein inside. The bubble glides right toward the ORANGE stack; the shared YELLOW energy glow brightens briefly (schematic). The GOLD route line extends behind it.
scenes.narration: Now the protein has to move. A vesicle, a small bubble of membrane, buds off the ER. It carries the protein across to the Golgi apparatus.

scenes.tts: The Golgi is a stack of flat sacs. It sorts the protein and packs it into new vesicles. There the protein waits until it is needed.
scenes.visual: Route strip: 'Golgi' lights up. The GOLD bubble merges with the first ORANGE sac; the glow passes sac by sac through the stack. At the far side, new GOLD bubbles bud off, each holding glowing protein, and gather near the membrane in a small cluster labelled 'stored, ready'.
scenes.narration: The Golgi is a stack of flat sacs. It sorts the protein and packs it into new vesicles. There the protein waits until it is needed.

scenes.tts: At the last stop, a vesicle meets the cell membrane. The two membranes fuse. The vesicle opens to the outside, and insulin is released.
scenes.visual: Route strip: 'vesicle' then 'cell membrane' light up. One GOLD bubble touches the GREY membrane; the two outlines merge into one continuous line, the bubble flattens into the membrane, and the GOLD glow spills outside the cell. Label: 'vesicle fuses with membrane'. The membrane does not open by itself; only the fusing bubble releases the glow.
scenes.narration: At the last stop, a vesicle meets the cell membrane. The two membranes fuse. The vesicle opens to the outside, and insulin is released.

scenes.tts: None of this is free. Building a protein chain and moving vesicles both use energy. Much of that energy comes as A T P, a small molecule cell parts can use. Mitochondria release energy from sugar and store it in A T P.
scenes.caption: None of this is free. Building a protein chain and moving vesicles both use energy. Much of that energy comes as ATP, a small molecule cell parts can use. Mitochondria release energy from sugar and store it in ATP.
scenes.visual: Pull back to the whole cell. RED mitochondria below the route light up. A small sugar cube icon enters one mitochondrion; YELLOW sparks labelled 'ATP' stream out into a shared glowing pool labelled 'energy supply (schematic)' that spreads under the whole route.
scenes.narration: None of this is free. Building a protein chain and moving vesicles both use energy. Much of that energy comes as ATP, a small molecule cell parts can use. Mitochondria release energy from sugar and store it in ATP.

scenes.tts: Now look at the whole route. The nucleus sends out a copy. Then the protein moves: rough E R, vesicle, Golgi, vesicle, cell membrane.
scenes.caption: Now look at the whole route. The nucleus sends out a copy. Then the protein moves: rough ER, vesicle, Golgi, vesicle, cell membrane.
scenes.visual: The full route line is solid: PURPLE from nucleus to ER, GOLD from ER to membrane. Each stop on the route strip lights in turn as it is named, in sync with the matching part in the cell. The YELLOW energy pool glows steadily beneath the whole route.
scenes.narration: Now look at the whole route. The nucleus sends out a copy. Then the protein moves: rough ER, vesicle, Golgi, vesicle, cell membrane.

scenes.tts: Notice what a route like this means. Each part can only work on what the part before it hands over. So every step depends on the one before it.
scenes.visual: Hand icons appear at each stop: the nucleus passes a purple strand to the ER; from there each stop passes the glowing gold parcel to the next, left to right. Small arrows between stops point one way only. Caption on screen: 'each part works only on what the part before hands over'.
scenes.narration: Notice what a route like this means. Each part can only work on what the part before it hands over. So every step depends on the one before it.

scenes.tts: So how does insulin get out of the cell? No single part does it. A copy of the gene leaves the nucleus, and the protein is handed from part to part. Mitochondria supply much of the A T P.
scenes.caption: So how does insulin get out of the cell? No single part does it. A copy of the gene leaves the nucleus, and the protein is handed from part to part. Mitochondria supply much of the ATP.
scenes.visual: Return to the opening frame: lock on the nucleus, GOLD glow outside the cell. The question mark between them is replaced by the solid route line, purple then gold, with RED mitochondria and the YELLOW energy pool beneath it.
scenes.narration: So how does insulin get out of the cell? No single part does it. A copy of the gene leaves the nucleus, and the protein is handed from part to part. Mitochondria supply much of the ATP.

scenes.visual: End card with the logo hexagon character holding a small gold parcel: 'Each part can only work on what the part before hands over.'
